{
  "question_intent": "Assess bank earnings-call responses on UKCB loan growth, margin expectations, through-the-cycle cost of risk, and cost efficiencies.",
  "main_topics": ["UKCB loan growth", "margin expectations", "through-the-cycle cost of risk", "cost efficiencies"],
  "answer_completeness": "Complete",
  "response_stance": "Direct",
  "evidence_level": "High",
  "contains_numeric_evidence": true,
  "contains_forward_guidance": false,
  "narrative_alignment": "Aligned",
  "question_quote": "I guess if we start maybe with UKCB. So I guess there, the loan growth has been picking up in recent quarters. But I guess the question becomes what's the margin that you expect going forward in that business? I mean there is some increase in terms of going back to your natural market share, but how tough is it to actually do that without compromising margin? And then a second one on that, what's the through-the-cycle cost of risk? I think it's 35 basis points [is] what you're expecting now. But I guess on a bigger book with a bigger push, maybe that should be going up? And then a second one, maybe on the overall cost efficiencies. When those were issued, I guess, inflation expectations were arguably lower. Do you see any risk on that and whatever levers you would pull to maybe offset that?",
  "answer_quote": "Okay. Thank you, Michael. Let me start with UKCB. So, our objective here is to lend more and it forms a really key part of our £30 billion commitment and the [>5%] CAGR in lending beyond that. As I look at the lending that's being put down there, Michael, I see no deterioration in margin, and no deterioration in the risk profile. The thing that we look at is the delinquency grades, [there is] no change in that at all. And really, that's because of two reasons. The first is, clearly, we're coming from a situation where our loan-to-deposit ratio is so low. We have actively not lent to many of our clients in the past. And this is about really having a clear intention and determination to lend where appropriate. So roughly half of our lending is coming from new clients, half of it is coming from existing clients. And as those new clients come on board, they're not meaningfully changing any of the kind of risk profile that we see and the portfolio margin remains static. So what's driving that? Well, firstly, it's that intention and secondly, it's the capability that we are landing. So the thing that we've done so far is materially changed the loan process, and what that does is it gives both the client and the regional teams confidence in our ability and intent to lend. That's really improved the lending pipeline. The other thing that we have actually seen is that as we engage with those clients more fully, what we're seeing is [that] they're getting to a higher number of products much faster than we would have expected. So the 2024 cohort, as I look at them now, are actually exhibiting the same number of products that would have taken previously four to five years to get to. So just that increased engagement with the client is really helpful. All of this, of course, is before we land iPortal, so all of the technology is there. We expect to migrate the corporates through this year, and that really gives us the confidence that we continue this kind of momentum. Your second point on loan loss rate. So on the basis that we're not changing the portfolio mix in any meaningful way, we wouldn't expect to change that loan loss rate guidance. On cost efficiencies, we've gone through a period from 2024 to 2026 where we actually experienced fairly high levels of inflation because inflation reaches us typically on quite a lagged basis. If you think about our major stripes of cost: people, property, technology, you don't see an immediate inflationary transmission through to those costs, Michael, they tend to sort of lag a little. So actually, 2024 and 2025 were relatively high levels of inflation for us, 2024 in particular. So we'd expect inflation to come through on a lagged basis, and what we've done before is try to lean more into the growth efficiency targets that we have to try and manage that position. So at this point, I wouldn't change our targets. I would expect us to go harder after efficiencies to try and manage it wherever possible.",
  "reason": "The response directly addresses the bank's expectations for UKCB loan growth, margin, through-the-cycle cost of risk, and cost efficiencies, providing specific figures and future outlooks, thus fulfilling the question's request for assessment of these topics."
}
